title: Mario vs. Donkey Kong
description:
Run, jump, and backflip your way to rescuing the stolen Mini-Mario toys in this puzzling twist on Mario action. Obstacles like spikes, moving platforms, and falling bricks stand in your way—put your brain to work and figure out the best way to reach the Mini-Marios! You’ll have to master Color Switches, Warp Boxes, and more as the difficulty ramps up across more than 130 levels, including challenging Plus and Expert levels.

Tailor the challenge to your playstyle or bring a friend along in local multiplayer!

Seeking a laid-back experience? The newly-added Casual Style removes time limits and adds checkpoints so you can relax and think. Looking for a tough puzzle-platforming challenge? Classic Style has got you covered with the timed levels and one-hit defeats of the original Game Boy™ Advance game. But that’s not all—you can bring a friend along in the newly-added Two-Player Mode, which adds an extra objective for Mario and Toad to take on together!

A classic rivalry reignites with updated visuals, new levels, and more ways to play!

With overhauled graphics, music, and cutscenes, this revitalized classic is looking better than ever. But wait—there’s more! Not only do you get new ways to play with Casual Style and Two-Player Mode, you also get two brand new worlds: Merry Mini-Land and Slippery Summit! That’s two new worlds, each with eight levels (and even more Plus levels), featuring new environments, enemies, and mechanics. And that’s not all! When you finish with those, you can test your skills in a newly-added Time Attack mode that will push your puzzle-platforming speed to the limit!

gameplayPillars.title: Puzzle-platforming
gameplayPillars.description: Every stage asks you to observe hazards, plan movement and use Mario’s acrobatics to retrieve the Mini-Marios.

gameplayPillars.title: Multiple play styles
gameplayPillars.description: Classic Style recreates a more demanding arcade feel, while Casual Style lowers frustration for newer players.

gameplayPillars.title: Local co-op
gameplayPillars.description: A second player can join as Toad and help solve the stages on the same system.

gameplayPillars.title: Puzzle-platform precision
gameplayPillars.description: Stages focus on timing, switches, keys, ladders, and object interactions, rewarding observation and careful movement more than speed.

gameplayPillars.title: Co-op and new content in the remake
gameplayPillars.description: The Nintendo Switch version adds local co-op support and extra content, giving the classic puzzle-platform formula more replay value.

worldSummary: Donkey Kong steals the Mini-Marios from the toy factory, sending Mario across a sequence of puzzle-platforming worlds full of enemies, switches, traps and collectible challenges. The Switch remake expands the content with new worlds, co-op and updated visuals.

storyChapters.title: Mini-Marios stolen
storyChapters.body: Donkey Kong grabs every Mini-Mario toy from the factory, triggering Mario’s chase.

storyChapters.title: Solve the stages
storyChapters.body: Mario clears stage after stage by collecting keys, avoiding hazards and guiding the Mini-Marios to safety.

storyChapters.title: Face Donkey Kong again
storyChapters.body: At the end of each world, Mario battles Donkey Kong in platforming boss encounters that test what you learned.

storyChapters.title: Chase Donkey Kong across themed worlds
storyChapters.body: After Donkey Kong steals Mini-Mario toys, Mario pursues him through themed stages filled with hazards, puzzles, and toy-rescue objectives.

storyChapters.title: Rescue toys and clear extra content
storyChapters.body: Later stages build on the core formula with trickier puzzle rooms, expert-level solutions, and replay-friendly objectives for careful players.

features: New two-player co-op and new worlds on Switch
Careful puzzle solving rather than pure platform speed
Local co-op helps make the remake more accessible
Short stages make it ideal for portable stop-and-start play

faq.a: Yes. It is a Switch remake of the Game Boy Advance title with new visuals, co-op and extra content.
The game supports one or two players on a single system.
It blends platforming movement with puzzle-solving, making every stage feel like a small challenge box.

faq.q: Does Mario vs. Donkey Kong have multiplayer?
faq.a: Yes. The Nintendo Switch remake includes local co-op support, allowing two players to work together through the puzzle-platform stages.

faq.q: Is it an action platformer or a puzzle game?
faq.a: It is primarily a puzzle-platformer. Movement matters, but most stages are built around planning routes, using objects, and solving room layouts.

verdictSummary: Overall score: 8.1/10. Strengths include Clever stage design; Excellent remake presentation; Co-op and accessibility options. Main drawbacks include Relatively compact scope; Not every challenge is equally inventive.
verdictPros: Excellent fit for short play sessions
Puzzle variety stays engaging across worlds
verdictCons: Not every challenge is equally inventive
Less action-focused than many Mario platformers
Completionists may need patience for late-stage puzzles
